## Welcome {#home}

### Leprosy

**Learning Objectives:**

- Describe the agent, transmission, and clinical classification of leprosy
- Distinguish paucibacillary from multibacillary disease
- Describe multidrug therapy (MDT) and its duration by type
- Outline India's NLEP and the SPARSH campaign
- Explain the role of deformity grading and stigma reduction

🟢 **MUST KNOW** · 🟡 **SHOULD KNOW** · 🟣 **MAY KNOW** · 🧡 **QUESTION**

::: {.notes}
Leprosy is a classic example of Chapter 23's sociological lens on
stigma — a curable disease whose social consequences have historically
outweighed its clinical severity in shaping patients' lives. This
module pairs the clinical/programmatic detail with that context.
:::

## Lecture 24: Leprosy Epidemiology and Classification {background-color="#E6EEF5"}

📚 **Lecture 24 of 28** · **CM8-CD.L24**

*Leprosy I - epidemiology and classification*

---

## Agent, Transmission, and Classification {background-color="#E3F2E1"}

🟢 **MUST KNOW**

**Agent:** *Mycobacterium leprae*, a slow-growing acid-fast bacillus
with an unusually long incubation period (average 3–5 years, up to
20).

**Transmission:** thought to occur mainly via **prolonged close
contact**, through nasal droplets from untreated multibacillary cases;
casual contact carries very low risk.

**Clinical classification (WHO, for treatment purposes):**

| Type | Skin lesions | Bacillary load |
|---|---|---|
| **Paucibacillary (PB)** | 1–5 lesions | Skin smear-negative |
| **Multibacillary (MB)** | 6 or more lesions | Skin smear-positive |

**Why this classification matters:** it directly determines which MDT
regimen and duration a patient receives (next slide) — the single most
consequential grouping in leprosy management.

---

## Multidrug Therapy (MDT) {background-color="#E3F2E1"}

🟢 **MUST KNOW**

WHO-recommended multidrug therapy, provided **free of cost** in India:

- **Paucibacillary (PB):** Rifampicin + Dapsone, for **6 months**
- **Multibacillary (MB):** Rifampicin + Clofazimine + Dapsone, for
  **12 months**

**Why multiple drugs, always:** monotherapy historically led to rapid
drug resistance — the same rationale already introduced for
tuberculosis (previous module) applies here, and MDT has been the
cornerstone of leprosy elimination globally since the 1980s.

**Leprosy is fully curable** with completed MDT — the disability
associated with it results from **delayed diagnosis and treatment**,
not from the disease being inherently untreatable.

---

## Deformity Grading and Disability Prevention {background-color="#FFF6DA"}

🟡 **SHOULD KNOW**

*M. leprae* has a particular affinity for **peripheral nerves and
skin**, which is why untreated leprosy can cause sensory loss and
deformity if not caught early:

| Grade | Findings |
|---|---|
| **Grade 0** | No sensory loss, no visible deformity |
| **Grade 1** | Sensory loss present, but no visible deformity |
| **Grade 2** | Visible deformity or damage present (e.g. clawing, ulcers, lagophthalmos) |

**Why early detection matters so much:** deformity results from nerve
damage that has already occurred by the time it's visible — this is
why active case-finding (next slide) aims to catch cases at Grade 0/1,
before irreversible damage sets in.

## Lecture 25: NLEP and SPARSH {background-color="#E6EEF5"}

📚 **Lecture 25 of 28** · **CM8-CD.L25**

*Leprosy II - NLEP and the SPARSH campaign*

---

## NLEP and SPARSH {background-color="#FFF6DA"}

🟡 **SHOULD KNOW**

India's **National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP)** has run since
1983, shifting emphasis from vertical campaigns to integration with the
general health system (the same NRHM-era integration logic already
seen for other vertical programmes, Chapter 11).

- **Active case-finding campaigns** — house-to-house surveys in
  high-endemic areas to detect cases early, before Grade 2 disability
  develops
- **SPARSH (Sensitize, Prevent, Awareness, Reach, Sanitize, Health)
  Leprosy Awareness Campaign** — a public awareness initiative
  specifically targeting **stigma reduction**, run annually around
  World Leprosy Day
- **Contact tracing and post-exposure prophylaxis** — single-dose
  rifampicin (SDR-PEP) offered to close contacts of newly diagnosed
  cases

**Direct link to Chapter 23:** leprosy is named there as a condition
where social consequences of diagnosis can outweigh clinical severity —
SPARSH exists precisely to address that structural stigma barrier.

## Self-Check: Question 1 {background-color="#FDE8E8"}

🧡 **QUESTION**

::: {.quiz-question}
### Question 1

A patient with 8 skin lesions and a skin-smear-positive result is
classified as:

- Paucibacillary (PB)
- [Multibacillary (MB)]{.correct data-explanation="6 or more skin lesions with a smear-positive result defines multibacillary (MB) leprosy, requiring the longer 12-month MDT regimen."}
- Grade 0
- Grade 1
:::
